_comment: Rating tier cut points per account, FROZEN by hand. Not recomputed at build time on purpose: deriving them from the live distribution would make pin colours shift every month as new posts land. `cuts` are the lower bounds of tiers 2..N on that account's own 0-5 scale, ascending; N-1 cuts give N tiers. Regenerate the evidence with `python scripts/calibrate.py --report`, read data/calibration_report.json, then edit this file.

born2eat_taiwan.note: His own vocabulary, not a statistic — 4.3 願意再訪, 4.6 愛店. They happen to fall almost exactly on quintiles of his distribution (top 77.7 / 58.3 / 38.0 / 22.3%), which is why the same percentile framing carries over to another reviewer.

jc_foodidi.note: Four tiers, not five: 45.9% of his restaurants sit on the single value 3.75, and no cut can split one value. Each tier is therefore one score he actually uses. His top tier is 8.8% against born2eat's 22% because he rarely goes above 4.0 — on the 99 venues both reviewed he scored lower on 94, mean -0.53. That is why the scales are kept separate: applying born2eat's 4.6 cut here would leave jc with no favourites at all.
